$purpose: Plugins the kit's OWN CI installs on every pull request (kit.yml's `plugins` job), on top of `.rocketflare.json` `defaultPlugins` — which is what a fresh clone installs, and is empty: analytics is opt-in. A plugin here is a canary, not a default: analytics has the most tables, cubes, crons and UI of any plugin, so a kit change that breaks an installed plugin fails here, on the kit PR, rather than at the plugins repo's next unrelated pull request. `kit:release` refuses a version an entry is not ready for, exactly as it does for a default plugin. `ref` is a release tag of either form: a plugin's own `<id>-vX.Y.Z` (per-plugin versions, #181) or a lockstep `X.Y.Z` (how the plugins repository released through 3.14.0); a bare `X.Y.Z` resolves to `<id>-vX.Y.Z` when that tag exists, and no `ref` means the plugin's newest release of either form. Kit-only: the rename deletes this file.
